newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks fly home on record turnover.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks fly home on record turnover.

text.p: SPI Futures 2385 +51 US 30yr 6.59 -0.11
10yrbond futs 92.525 +0.115 Gold NY 369.25 Lon fix 369.60
*Stocks sprint home to higher close. Choppy BHP trade dictates tone. Option exercises boost volume. Volume 495.84 million, value A$1.73 bln, 1073 stocks traded, 288 steady, 521 up, 264 down.
Australian shares sprinted home in the afternoon to close sharply higher on Friday as strong buying interest late in the day ensured a positive response to the Dow's second highest finish ever.
In turnover terms, the Australian market set new records with A$1.73 billion worth of shares traded, surpassing the previous record of A$1.6 billion on June 28, 1996.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 42.1 points higher at 2,373.8.
December share price index futures were up 51 points at 2,385, an 11.2 point premium to the index.

While some early Dow-inspired gains were dissipated by choppy trading in BHP by the midsession, further analysis of the market leader's 9.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$790 million saw buyers return in the afternoon.
"It took a long time to wind itself up but when it did it went quite nicely," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse, pointing to volatile trade in the bellwether stock.
"BHP was all over the shop with people not knowing what to make of the result."
With a soaring Dow and stronger metals prices though, the day's gains were what traders should have expected, Sekely said.
"The rise is no more or no less than what you would expect on the back of a strong Wall Street and very good metal prices so anything less would have been a disappointment," he said.
Despite the imminent Christmas break, interest remained strong and Sekely said further gains could eventuate next week.
"These things are hard to pick but December is traditionally strong and it could run on yet. There was quite strong buying towards the end of the day."
While option exercises prior to official opening were worth about A$800 million, the remaining A$900 million of the day's trade suggested plenty of buyers were still interested.

In other local markets, the Australian bond market spent another session mainly marking time ahead of the year-end holidays, although yields were sharply lower reflecting renewed strength in U.S. Treasuries. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.39 percent.

The Australian dollar posted its highest local close since the Reserve Bank cut interest rates last week and although a move to US$0.8000 was on the cards, traders said a thin market exaggerated the move upwards. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT) the Australian dollar had edged up to US$0.7955/60, up on an early US$0.7941/46 and a Thursday close of US$0.7925/30.
"Some turnover was options-related but there was a bit of genuine activity there today," Sekely said.
Outside of BHP, transport and logistics group Brambles attracted attention with offshore investor interest pushing its shares to a record high of A$24.00.
Rises outnumbered falls by ratio of about two to one, while about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active in line with BHP trade while options activity slowed after Thursday's expiry.
Total options traded 43,927 (60,476)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 10,987 (5,459)
